$comment: Recorded pack sizes, refreshed 2026-09-14 and the refresh is the story. `check:artifacts` existed, `artifact-size-ratchet-lock.test.ts` unit-tested its verdict function against synthetic inputs, and **no workflow ever ran the verdict against the real packages** — so seven of them drifted past this file unchallenged: closeout +268%, seniority +112%, paratext +87%, burgee +51%, caique +46%, flagstaff +15%, linegauge +11%. The growth is explained — the PLAN 1.1 schema fold put a 6.5 KB family schema in every package that reaches the plugin registry, and waves 1 and 3 added plugin hosts and drop-in façades — but explaining growth is not the same as accepting it, which is why the numbers are named here rather than quietly replaced. `npm run lint` runs the check now, so the next one is caught. seniority moved 2026-09-20, deliberately and in one direction: 47,616 -> 59,124 gzipped and 153,040 -> 193,682 unpacked, +24.2% and +26.6%. The cause is two drop-in subpaths that did not exist — `seniority/lilconfig` (lilconfig 3.1.3's surface, which took its compat row from 0 / 77 to 67 / 77) and `seniority/rc` (rc 1.2.8's merge without its four dependencies). Both are product, not drift, and the package's own R9 ceiling in `shape.test.ts` — 140,000 B of built `dist`, measured against lilconfig — is still met. The band is raised here rather than the ceiling there, because they measure different things: this one is the tarball a consumer downloads, that one is the graph a bundler walks. **Lowered 2026-09-21, and this direction needs no permission.** `scripts/strip-comments.mjs` read only the top level of `dist/`, so every nested entry point shipped its doc comments: burgee unpacked 949,221 -> 635,640 (-33.0%) and flagstaff 200,204 -> 188,624 the moment it recursed. A ratchet tightening is always free; it is the loosening that is a decision. **2026-09-21: `linegauge` and `seniority` were the two published packages whose build never ran `strip-comments` at all** — not a recursion gap, simply absent from their `build` script. Adding it: linegauge unpacked 83,538 -> 56,148 (-32.8%), seniority 193,682 -> 139,793 (-27.8%). Both directions of this file's history now have the same cause: a stripper that was not reaching what it was supposed to reach.
